utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Today for the first session we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, with Judge Lattanzi being away due to her urgent personal matters. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon. I wanted to raise in the absence of Mr. Poparic a couple of issues that arose yesterday as a result of the 19 items that we were notified of after the witness began his evidence in chief. We've had now an opportunity to review those items that were -- that we're able to read and the material includes four videos, two transcripts, some documents, some tables, and some photos. A review of that material, Your Honours, has given rise to some concerns on my part with respect to both the scope of what this witness's evidence is intended to be and with regard to the late notification of these documents. The late notification in these circumstances -- in fact, the late notification of these documents is so blatant, Your Honour, I think it affects seriously some of the basic principles of fairness, particularly when we're dealing with an expert witness. I'd just like to recall a little bit of what happened yesterday. The first -- when the first of these late documents was dealt with with Mr. Poparic, I let the matter go by, thinking that this was inadvertence, but then we saw the second document come up which was a video, 65 ter number 1D07465, and that led to a discussion of an unscheduled incident which was -- which turned out to be an attempt to refer back to a scheduled incident, G6, which was not discussed in this witness's report. Effectively, in my submission, an attempt to re-open the testimony of Mrs. Subotic, an expert who's already testified and to re-open that in an inappropriate means. So now just putting that in context, I'd like to turn to the documents. First of all, two of them are already exhibits. That's 1D07469 is D2431, and 1D07470 is D2430. Now, another two of these documents deal with unscheduled shelling incidents that are also not within the scope of either of Mr. Poparic's two reports, the inconsistencies report and the small arms report. One of them, 1D07847, appears to be an untranslated copy of an investigative file regarding shelling incident in Gradacacka Street in Sarajevo on 3 July 1995. 1D07473, which is also untranslated and largely illegible, appears to deal with another shelling incident on 21 November 1994. Neither of these two documents have anything to do with Mr. Poparic's two reports on their face. So in my submission if this witness is going to offer expert evidence on these or other such unscheduled incidents, that is tantamount to his effectively preparing or creating a new report without complying with any of the applicable notice provisions in the rules. And furthermore, Your Honours have already in your decision of 12 March 2013 excluded a supplementary report prepared by this witness dealing with unscheduled incidents on the basis that detailed evidence going to those unscheduled incidents is unhelpful. So with respect to these two documents, that looks, Your Honours, to the Prosecution like an effort to circumvent Your Honours' ruling. So, in my submission, those two documents, the use of those two documents should not be permitted. Now, two of the other documents, 1D07464 and 1D02358, are charts, untranslated, commenting on documents prepared by organs of the Ministry of the Interior. They each relate to what appears to be 41 unscheduled incidents. It's unclear whether these tables contain information provided by the witness or the witness's comments, and in fact Dr. Karadzic attempted to tender one of these tables, that would be 1D02358, through the witness Ekrem Suljevic more than two years ago. And that can be found, or the discussion of that can be found at transcript pages 6152 to 6157. Now, Your Honours, if you look at that testimony, as we've done, and the surrounding discussion, it appears that at least 1D02358 could be a document purporting to analyse some aspect - I don't know what that might be - but the regularity of these records prepared by these organs. They are, in my submission, Your Honour, totally inappropriate for use with this witness, first, because if that's what they are - and we don't know - they're not within the demonstrated or the notified scope of this witness's expertise at all. He's a ballistics expert. His CV does not show he was ever a member of the security services, any arm of the justice ministry in Bosnia and Herzegovina. His CV does not show that he has any specialised knowledge or expertise in the work methods of those organs, in record-keeping practices, or document authentication. Also, these documents aren't mentioned in his reports, either of them. And frankly, if this evidence had formed part of the report that we received notification of, the Prosecution would have applied for its exclusion when we filed our motion in regard to those reports in February of this year. And again, referring to Your Honours' decision on that motion of March 2013, Your Honours noted that the witness in these reports commented on numerous matters -- pardon me, in relation to the small arms report, commented on numerous matters unrelated to his small arms expertise, including the authenticity of medical and police records. So, in my submission, use of these tables and the underlying documents should in these circumstances also not be permitted. Two other documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. How many documents are we dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Each table has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, you said two documents -- you dealt with two documents already admitted and then two documents you're objecting to and then another two. And then -- because we haven't received the entire document -- number of documents. How many documents were disclosed to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: 19 all together. Two were dealt with in court yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I have specific issues with respect to a number of them, and I'll be asking for Your Honours' accommodation with respect to photographs and videos. And my colleague will be able to give me the numbers in a few moments because I don't have those for you as I speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, maybe this could be a helpful intervention. So actually the use of those documents yesterday was as much of a surprise to me as they were to the Prosecution, and I think our game plan with this witness was to go through the sniping incidents one by one. And I spoke to Dr. Karadzic this afternoon and he's prepared to do that with the commencement of the testimony. And whether or not any of those other documents are used with this witness is up in -- is still being debated. So I suggest that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, why could not that have been communicated to the Prosecution first without having to lose some time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we just received their e-mail before court and I just discussed this with Dr. Karadzic five minutes before court started when I first had contact with him after receiving notice that they were going to object. So this is -- I could have interrupted her a little earlier, I realise that, but I wanted to be somehow polite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But off the top of my head, I have general sympathy with what -- about the concern Ms. Edgerton expressed. I just looked at the wording of Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I understand completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: And I think it's better if we focus on the report, the sniping, and I hope that it won't be necessary to use those documents. But if Dr. Karadzic at the end of that feels it's necessary to insist, we could advise everyone and we could proceed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In the interests of efficiency then, I think we should proceed. But, Your Honours, with respect to the photos that we were notified of - and I'll be able to have the numbers for you in a moment but I'm sure Dr. Karadzic knows which ones we're speaking of - they relate to sniping incidents F4, as we can see, and F10. With respect to the videos, one of those videos relates to sniping incident F12. In light of -- and I can give you the 65 ter numbers of the videos now: 1D7457, 1D7460, 1D7458, and 1D7459. My colleague will provide me with the 65 numbers for the photographs. But anyway, to get back to this. Because of the late -- the belated notice of these documents, we would ask that Your Honours consider recommending to Dr. Karadzic that he deal with F4, F10, F12 at the outset so that would allow us extra time to prepare for the cross-examination in relation to that material. So if he could deal with those first, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or he may not deal with those photos or videos.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you follow, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm confused. I don't know whether I'm to deal with that first or whether not to deal with that first. I don't know. F4, F10, F12, and F17, all these are video-clips, so I would like to seek your guidance as to how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has general concerns that you are using with this expert that is included in the witness report -- expert report. Our Rule says: "The full statement and/or report of any expert witness to be called by a party shall be disclosed within the time-limit prescribed by the Trial Chamber or by the Pre-Trial Judge." In the circumstances there may be cases you can supplement the witness's report by a small number of exhibits, but by extensively relying on undisclosed documents you are circumventing the Rules. So the rule is that -- the rule is clear. If you are planning to tender or show -- use those documents, I'm sorry, video or photos, with Mr. Poparic, you should do that at the outset so that the Prosecution have time for preparation; otherwise, that means if you are not going to use those photos or videos, you may proceed as you like.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. I just want to tell you what governed me in taking the opportunity or having this witness before us, he was affiliated with the military industry in Sarajevo and he is familiar with Sarajevo. What concerns me is whether in the adjudicated facts there are the consequences of the excluded incidents or the testimonies and materials of the witnesses whose materials have not been admitted according to 92 quater. I'm simply not sure that I shouldn't touch upon the incidents which are not in the indictment because they may have been included in the indictment albeit in a different form or way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a totally different area raised by Ms. Edgerton. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will start with the incidents and when we have exhausted that I will seek your leave to present other things, if the need for that arises by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The same rule applies today. Let's make breaks between questions and answers and let's both of us speak slowly. I would like to start by referring to incident 4 described in your report. Do you have the report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of e-court, 7902 is the 1D number of this report. Can it be called up in e-court because we will need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, could you please tell us the essence of what the physical evidence on the ground and the truth of the incident, what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened on the 3rd of September, 1993, in Ivana Krndelja Street, currently it is Aziza Sacirbegovic Street. On that occasion a mother and a daughter were wounded. There was just one hit. Based on the testimony of the wounded person, several other hits were made which means that there was a burst of fire, there were short bursts of fire. The same round hit both a mother and a daughter. There is no medical evidence to that effect. There was no forensic investigation. Based on the statement of the wounded person, it was established that she had been crossing the street together with her daughter. There was a barrier composed of containers on that road, and that protected them from a view from Ozrenska Street. When she had made one and a half steps onto the street, she was hit, but that was one and a half steps after the containers. That's when she was hit. Based on that we carried out an analysis of the distance between the positions of the VRS in Ozrenska Street and we established that the smallest distance to that place was about 680 metres. Based on the video-clip that was recorded by the Prosecutor's office, we measured the time that was required for that person to cross the distance between the shelter and the place where she was hit. We did not reduce that time because she started walking from a certain place and in the real situation that time was somewhat shorter, but we simply ignored that. Based on the characteristics of the ammunition that may have been used, we established that the time that she needed to cross the distance between the containers and the place of the incident was less than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could the parties help me locate the relevant pages in the report?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Page 52 in the English version of the report, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the way, I again note that images and figures were omitted from the English translation. I would like the -- those images and figures to be inserted in the English translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Last time you ordered the language section to do that, so if you could make that same order I'm sure they'll comply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian version this starts on page 71. Can we call up 1D07463 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you refer to that document when you're providing your answer. Can you please finish while we're waiting.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time needed by the round that was fired from the position of the VRS in Ozrenska Street to the place of the incident was more than the time needed by the person to cross from the container to the place where it was hit. In other words, the fire had to be opened before she became visible to the shooter in order for that bullet to hit her in that place, which means that she was not intentionally targeted either by the VRS or whoever from another place. I am talking about the shortest distance from the place of the incident to the position of the VRS. In that area there is no optical visibility; in other words, the place of the incident could not be seen from those positions. I knew from the materials that we were provided with that there was a photo. It was claimed that that photo was taken from the place from which fire was opened; however, it was an enlarged photo and I couldn't establish exactly where that photo was taken from. However, I did recognise some of the facilities there and I realised that the photo was taken a bit further to the east at the positions where the Serbian positions were even further away from that place. That's why I excluded that place from my investigation because I didn't have the complete information. When Slobodan, whose family name I can't remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tusevljak?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Slobodan Tusevljak testified, the Prosecution showed that photo as well as the photo of the place from which the photo was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Could you please mark Ozrenska Street in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and the accused please be asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be helped with the electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you please not overlap each other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I asked the witness to mark.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the place of the incidents. Am I to mark it with number 1? Is that what you wanted me to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now could you please mark Ozrenska Street, and in this regard I would like you to mark both the Serbian and the Muslim positions.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be Ozrenska Street approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. To be clear, is this one of the photos that was added later on?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I write Ozrenska?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The question was inaudible by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now take the red pen and mark the Serbian positions.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have been here approximately. Those were the most forward positions more or less, and based on the map that we had at our disposal they should have been somewhere around here. There was a forward position here, and that's the shortest distance from the place of the incident to the Serbian positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For the transcript I have to say that the pen is blue because it says in the transcript that the pen is red. Can you put number 3 next to the line, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where are the Muslim positions?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim positions were somewhere below approximately here based on the maps, somewhere around here they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record, did you put number 2 for Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now number 4 for the Muslim positions in the area.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, in the closest of the scenarios what is the distance between the Serbian positions and the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can draw a line to mark that distance, and that would be about 680 metres. Maybe the best thing for me to do would be to write "600 metres" next to the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is where the most forward positions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the visibility? But you can't see it here. Can you see a facility on this Google Earth map that you can recognise, one that we can also recognise in the photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What photo do you have in mind? There are a lot of facilities that I might be able to mark for you. For example, this facility here or this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put numbers 5 and 6 to those -- next to those circles and tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 5 is a damaged house in Triglavska Street, and I'm going to mark another building and I'll put a number 7 next to it. That's a building that we can also see on the photo. Number 6 is a private house that we can see in one -- in some of the photos. And based on that -- the position of that house, we can establish where those positions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to sign this and put a date on this document.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So today we are 29 May; right? I apologise, can I mark another place? I don't want to have to come back to this document. I would like to mark it by number 8. This is the place from which the photo that I've mentioned was taken. Obviously that was according to my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted as a document?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We haven't heard Dr. Karadzic put one single question to the witness about the basis for his knowledge in the markings that he's made on this map, so I would object until some foundation is established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, or could you answer the question, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can answer. Mr. Karadzic started by saying something and then obviously interrupted me -- I interrupted him. I mentioned a few photographs that were shown to the witness Slobodan Tusevljak which are directly connected to this incident, and in those photos we recognise some of the facilities and we can establish the place from which those photos were taken. And in this document this is marked by number 8. That was the whole point of this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you inspect those places?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I know this place from before, and when I saw those photos I asked the Defence to send me those photos which they did. And then on the 12th of December, last year, which was 2012, I went to the site. I walked along Varazdinska Street in order to personally see what kind of an area or a ground it was and whether those facilities were there. My main objective was to see where the photos were taken from in order to be able to establish whether the distance was bigger or smaller than the distance that I was able to establish based on the time of the flight of the round, whether that distance was more than 680 metres, and that was the main objective of my visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many times did you inspect the place?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I inspected the place several times, many times, as a matter of fact, because my wife lived very close to number 6. So I'm very familiar with the area. I knew it from before the war. I know the neighbourhood and the people living there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this ever admitted? Has it got a number? Because I would like to call up photo 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic had this witness mark confrontation lines and military positions. So absent evidence that the witness was there at the time, I think it would be useful for us to hear the basis or the foundation for those markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. It's not for you, Mr. Poparic. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This information is in the report of the witness, so I don't think that it's necessary for him to orally give the basis of everything that he's illustrating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I believe in his report he indicated that -- he could point to the exact page but he indicated where the confrontation lines were, what the distance was between the place, and where it would have had to have been fired from if it was in the Serb positions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's that para number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Poparic can give that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's photo 49, paragraph 59, if that may be of any assistance. I believe it's 59.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Photo 48 is very similar in terms of its Google presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm fine with using the images contained in his report. But while I'm hearing his evidence, his evidence looks like that of an investigator, not of an expert. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, we're not seeing those lines at all that you referred to. Can you help us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Baird. On page 55 of the English, on the top paragraph, number -- paragraph 59, he says: "According to the operations map, the separation line ..." And then he describes where the separation line existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this map, but bear in mind that -- how much probative value it will have, Mr. Karadzic, given that he's not a fact witness. Please proceed. Shall we assign the number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number would be D3616, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please take a look at the image that was shown to Mr. Tusevljak. I have it as 1D1746. It is already in evidence. 1D07468. Thank you. Mr. Poparic, can you tell us what this picture represents and where was it taken from?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph I mentioned as having in my files and originally I couldn't tell where it had been taken from, but now based on other photographs I can tell that this picture was taken from Ozrenska Street. The building to the right is the one I marked as number 6 on that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then please mark it here as well.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll mark it with a number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you switch on the pen yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is building number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the incident site with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us how did you conclude that this photograph was taken east of the axis of the street?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell based on that map and another photograph that was shown to that witness, but it's hard to tell based on this photograph. That's why I didn't consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Given that this is on the right, what is the distance between the Serbian positions and the incident site? Is it over or under 680 metres?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I measured some 730, 740 metres, I mean the place from where this picture was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sign and initial.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted so we can move on to the next?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No problem with that. And just for the record this was not shown to Mr. Tusevljak. This is 65 ter 23966 and he was shown 23967 and 23968, which are similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.text: Document receives number D3617, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very similar photograph; right? But the zoom is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is D2431 also for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give the number, Ms. Edgerton, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Was this photograph taken from the Serbian positions or is it zoomed in?
