utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3618, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D07470, please. I believe that this one was shown to Tusevljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, you told us this was also admitted. Do you have the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I can just see it on the screen, then I would probably be able to help.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D07470.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I found my own handwritten notes and I think it's D2430.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Upside down, please. Back one. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, please also switch on the pen and mark the house with number 6 and this incident site with number 1, and tell us where this was taken from.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph that was shown to Mr. Tusevljak, and that is when I first saw from where that zoomed-in photograph was taken. I'll mark that visible building with number 6 and I'll mark the incident site with 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this damaged house be seen elsewhere in some other photograph, I mean on the Google picture?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the brick house? I marked it with a number 7. This one with the foundation and the one next to it, they are finished now and people live in them. I marked them before. I believe it was marked number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it number 8. On the previous page you said "7." We should have clarified that, 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 7 after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay. Put a 7 next to it or cross out the number 8. Considering the position of the photographer, where were the Serbian positions, in front of him or behind him?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find that anywhere because I wasn't there. I can only say that in front of this building there is a slope and it's logical for the positions to be either here or a bit further back. This place is some 730 to 740 metres away from the incident site, and the positions are down there. But I don't know what the situation was like during the war because there was a wood here, which was cut down during the war. Whether it was here exactly, I don't know. But there is no reliable information as to whether there was a line of sight as we see it now back then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? And we'll see on D3676 whether it's 7 or 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please date it and initial.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be received as Exhibit D3619.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. There was just a gap that we were filling in, so the next exhibit number will be D3623, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at D3616 now so we can see whether that has number 7 or number 8. Perhaps we can have a split image so as to see both. Is this house number 8?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's 8. I made a mistake. I marked house number 6 -- it should have been 7. That's the mistake. I was marking on those zoomed-in photographs. I was putting there -- I was putting 6 there and it should have been 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, where there's a 6 in those photographs, it should be a 7?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you have also now said wherever there's a 7 in those photographs, it should be 8 here?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get D107472 on one half of the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you tell us the basis upon which you concluded number 8 is the very house we saw in the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell based on the previously shown photographs and on the position of the buildings that can be seen there and based on an inspection of the site. Only these two buildings can be the places where the photograph was taken. In front of that building there's a strong slope and it isn't logical for a firing position to be on that slope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we zoom in on number 8. Does it look like that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is enough. The one I'm pointing at now, I don't know if you can see it, is the house where -- that only had a foundation. The one on the left is a mere foundation, whereas the one next to it is half finished. And around them there are some orchards or something. We could see them in those photographs. There is also a flat surface there. That's the site where other houses were built subsequently. One of them was under construction at the time. We can see the roofs of the houses downhill and based on that we can determine the exact position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know when this Google image was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Google image in 2011, I believe, that's the most recent version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we zoom out and see the whole photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you, sir, would you please draw this 700-odd-metre-long line.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the point where the photograph was taken from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. From there to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark it with number 9, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an angle. I measured it on Google and it's between 10 and 15 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that BH army map, can this bend at number 3 be seen? Shall we show it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it can be seen more or less.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted with the same exhibit number? Just so that the red line is kept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be saved as it is now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have image 49, please, from the document. 1D7902, that's the document. That's the report. Serbian page 78. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please zoom in. We need to have the map enlarged. We no longer need the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, let's leave the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We may need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 3 that you marked there, as the line moves, yes. Can you mark number 3? Just a moment. Perhaps you can activate the pen yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the bend roughly. And how can we recognise this? Well, you see, I'm going to mark this with a number 4, that's fine, or maybe a bigger number.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10. The road here, there's this very small road here on the side, and that's why I thought that we should leave that photograph with the beginning of the road so it's easy to recognise on that basis where this is, this area that is protruding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Could you please use a red line to mark the line of taking the photograph. D1, could you use that to mark the site of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be here roughly. It's very small, isn't it, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can you show us the direction from which the picture was taken, 700-something metres?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a bit more to the right but it would be here roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put the date and your initials there.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your conclusion briefly, and why?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After these additional checks, the conclusion is that the lady who was wounded could not have been hit -- could not have been targeted intentionally because the bullet had to be fired before she appeared from behind the shelter. That is to say the person who was firing had to fire the bullet before he saw that person. Let me just say one more thing. When analysing the time, we did not take into account the time that was needed for the person who was firing to prepare for firing, and may I remind you that as far as sniper rifles are concerned it is 30 bullets per minute that is the maximum velocity. So at least a second and a bit more is needed to prepare for firing. So this is just the time that it takes the bullet to get there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this marked image.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course no objection to Your Honours receiving the marked image, but not as a map from the 14th Division Chief of Staff of the Bosnian Army land forces, because this is a map that's taken from 65 ter number 07048 which is a working map of the Main Staff of the command of the 12th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3624, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us another thing as a ballistics expert. What is the precision of a sniper rifle at this distance of 680 and 740 metres?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a sniper rifle at these distances, it is precise enough to be able to hit a person. Not the rifle, it's the marksman who can do that. This had to be a burst of gun-fire. That's what the witness said. According to the testimony of the injured party, it was not a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show 1D7472 on part of the screen, and on the other half of the screen image 44 from the document. First image 44 from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh, and, Your Honours, just with regard to the map we just spoke about and I took to my feet on, I'm advised by one of my colleagues it's -- I misinformed you. It's the Chief of Staff's map, not the Main Staff. And we'll check with Mr. Reid, but I think that map may be P1764. So I told Your Honours it was a map of the Main Staff of the command of the 12th Division, but I'm told it's the Chief of Staff's map of the command of the 12th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what is wrong with the report is that -- is the mistake of that number of the division?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On the left-hand side of image 44, could we just zoom in on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we see on this right-hand photograph, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a picture from the scene itself. We had to move a bit to the other side because of these trees, otherwise we couldn't see it. So you see along this line, the front part of a car, that was the place of the incident as was marked by this witness. And this is a view of Hrasno Brdo. Ozrenska Ulica is behind it and you cannot see it from this position. It's only from a photograph that was taken a lot further away from Omera Maslica Street. You can see another part where you can see Ozrenska Street. So this is proof -- I mean we dealt with that in detail, that this place was not visible from this forward position of the Army of Republika Srpska that we saw on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This zoom is even more than five times because in the document it was zoomed in five times. So can we remove the right-hand picture now. It's the same thing but less of a zoom; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the right-hand side has more of a zoom and the left-hand side has less. In image 45 you can see the difference better in terms of the visibility of Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 45, please, which is on the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Next page. 75 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The left-hand photograph is zoomed in five times as explained in image 44, and the right-hand photograph was taken at a distance that is far greater. Omera Maslica Street, I don't know what its name is now, and then there's street of Zmaja od Bosne. And these red lines mark the level that can be seen on the left-hand side and on the right, I mean the red line is the upper line of the photograph on the other side. So all of this, what you can see on the right-hand side, is not visible from the place where the incident occurred. And then up there there's Ozrenska Street and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- we established that this line corresponds to a distance of 580 metres. So the Serb positions were a further 100 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, at 740 metres there is visibility and at 680 there is not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not follow the witness. He started speaking too fast and too soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, the interpreters were not able to catch up with your speed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So from 680 metres the place of the incident is not visible. From 740 or 730 metres, it doesn't matter, it is visible. However, this is a photograph that was taken in 2000 or in 2001. During the war we don't know what the situation was because I know that that area was covered with a forest that was pretty big. The trees were 15 or 20 metres away, so I don't know whether this area was covered by that, I cannot confirm. But nearby there used to be a big forest that was cut down during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber how come you know that that area is -- well, actually you mentioned it but I'm not sure it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that my wife's parents lived in this street and I came there for many years and I met all of these people who lived there. And I knew the forest. And there used to be a motel there that was built during the Olympic games. It never worked, it was never opened, and so it remained in some photographs. And you can see the remains of this motel in some of the photographs, and I know that there used to be a forest there. And now we see that there is a road leading to Ozrenska. At that time there wasn't a road. There weren't quite a few roads there before the war. A lot of this was built after the war, roads, houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now focus on incident 10. What did you conclude as you studied the evidence related to number 10? It's page 123 in Serbian and I don't know which number it is in English. I know that the paragraph number is 134.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can somebody help me with this? Why did Madam Edgerton want 10? Do we have some new photograph there? I don't seem to be able to recall that. Which number of document would be a new one as regards this incident?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: One of the photographs that Dr. Karadzic just used with the witness. 1D07472.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As regards this incident we haven't got anything new.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But now that we've had this called up, can you tell us what you concluded?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the 22nd of July, 1994. The incident is interesting because in the indictment it says, and in all the other documents related to this incident, that it occurred in Miljenka Cvitkovica Street and all the evidence was adduced in Dzemela Bijedica Street. That is something that is highly illogical. Secondly, disregarding all of that, the fact that the locations do not tally, we looked at the police documents, primarily photo documents, and on the basis of that they concluded that the bullet was fired from Zagorska Street, which is now called --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In photo documentation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the name of the street. The bullet was fired from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to police assertions, Zagorska Street, now it's called Posavska Street. That's where the shot came.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have image 87 now from the document on page 127 in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this shows.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this shows the distance actually from this location in Dzemela Bijedica where this evidence was presented in terms of the incident having occurred there and the site in Posavska Street from where this shot could have come from. 1.245 metres is the distance and that exceeds the abilities even of a sniper rifle. So if the shot came from that location, it must have been a machine-gun because that would be the only weapon that would have that kind of range.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Mr. Karadzic spoke so we didn't understand either him or the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Your previous question was not translated. Could you repeat it all over.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked what this image represented.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This image represented the distance from Posavska Street to the site where the evidence was presented concerning this incident in Dzemela Bijedica Street. 1.245 metres is the distance involved which shows the following: If the targeting was intentional, if this boy was targeted intentionally, it couldn't have been a sniper rifle. It might have been a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please draw a line along Dzemela Bijedica Street and then two parallel ones, Miljenka Cvitkovica, perhaps you can use blue and red, where according to the findings of the police the incident occurred. Use the pen. Can we have that image back, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Dzemela Bijedica Street, one of the longest in Sarajevo. Maybe I extended the line too much, but it goes downwards in any case. It's a bit short -- actually, the right-hand side line should be shorter but it's neither near nor there. And Miljenka Cvitkovica is behind this building here. There is a huge and long building, the longest in Sarajevo probably, and behind it is Miljenka Cvitkovica Street. Miljenka Cvitkovica Street was certainly not visible from those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put the number 1 on Dzemala Bijedica Street and number 2 on Miljenka Cvitkovica Street.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In terms of the traces on the tarpaulin cover, what did you conclude?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it was: The police concluded that the bullet first fired from that street because they found a trace on the tarpaulin cover through which the bullet passed and then it shattered the glass on a cafe bar. And they say that by a projection they could establish that that's where the bullet was fired from. And I claim with full responsibility that that was not the case as I'm looking at these photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can we look at image 89. Does this mean that the boy was not visible if the bullet had to pierce the tarpaulin cover first?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say. They arrived at the conclusion that another bullet was fired which basically pierced the stall cover, but this is not proof enough to show that the boy was not visible. However, based on the traces on the tarpaulin cover and the glass on the coffee bar, they managed to establish the trajectory. As I'm looking at this photo, I don't know how they could see through the hole in the tarpaulin cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, could you put the date and sign the photo.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be admitted and then briefly before the break I would like to look at image 89.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3625, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what this image depicts.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It completely refutes the police claims. They drew their conclusions based on the traces on the awning on the right-hand side where you see the arrow. According to them this is the place where the bullet entered the awning and then continued its trajectory and shattered the glass on the coffee bar. However, this is not a bullet trace. This is damage which was caused by another object. I'm sure that all of us have torn our trousers and we know what that would look like. The trace of the bullet can be seen on the previous photo. That's where you can see something that looks like a bullet trace. When you look at that trace and the place where that bullet pierced the coffee bar window-pane, one arrives at the conclusion that that bullet had arrived from south-west, which is much further from the trajectory than the investigators established as the trajectory of that bullet. In addition to that, the incoming angle of that bullet when we look at the height of the tarpaulin and the place where the window-pane of coffee bar was pierced is about 40 to 45 degrees which could not have been the case. If the bullet had been fired from 1.200 metres from an infantry rifle, the angle would have been a couple of degrees. This trace could have been caused by a bullet in free fall, or somebody in the coffee bar actually fired a shot and that bullet came out through the window and hit the awning. In any case, the place that was traced by the police is not a bullet trace and it misled the police to arrive at an erroneous conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the trajectory -- or before that, who is it who drew the arrow?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was drawn by the police and it's based on their claim that this is a bullet trace. But this doesn't look like a bullet trace at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now would you please tell us, what would be the azimuth if the bullet had arrived from the direction which they claim it did, which would be less than 180, and what would be the others?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Off the cuff it's very difficult for me to say, but approximately it would be 40 degrees or perhaps even more and it would be more to the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we are not making enough pauses and maybe our interpreters are -- maybe we have tired out our interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So perhaps this would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break for half an hour and resume at three minutes after 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Just a small thing, Your Honour, for some cross-referencing. D3624 is an excerpt from P01764.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- was an exhibit marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, being a map excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It is an excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The original map -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now let's focus on incident number 12 which is described in paragraph 162. I don't know on which page in English; however, the paragraph is 162. The Serbian page is 141. Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Page 96 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We were not getting the translation. Could you repeat?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably it was only my headphones. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us based on the materials that were accessible to you and the physical evidence that you could study, what could you conclude about that incident?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That incident happened on the 18th of November, 1994. Dzenana Sokolovic and her son Nermin Divovic were hit. On that occasion she was wounded and her son was killed. Based on all the available facts, it was very difficult to establish as to what had indeed happened there. I believe that in that case we were missing a very important thing and that was a detailed forensic finding. The key to the solution of this case lies in the forensic expertise. That was one of those cases where it was practically impossible to establish correctly what had happened without a detailed forensic finding. In the file there is an excerpt from the forensic finding; however, we don't know what that is, whether that was just a post mortem examination or a post mortem finding and there is a big difference between the two because a finding will include the details of the examination of the victim's body with all the necessary details, whereas an examination is just as it says, an examination, and a statement as to how the person died. Here we have a lot of contradictory data and primarily this concerns the trajectory or the direction from which the bullet was fired. Whether it hit the mother and the son from the right to the left or from the left to the right and the latter we can find in the police report and the medical documents after Dzenana Sokolovic's surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us what does the first medical report say, the most recent or the earliest one after the wounding? Where were the entry and exit wounds in those two people?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dzenana Sokolovic's discharge letter it says that she was wounded, or rather, that the entry wound is on the left and the exit wound is on the right. And in that the doctor also provided the dimensions of the entry and exit wounds which correspond to the phenomenon because an entry wound is always smaller and the exit wound is always larger, and that was the case here as well. In the case of her son Nermin Divovic, it says in the police report that they had received information from the hospital that he was hit from the left and that the exit wound was on the right-hand side. These are the two official documents which testify to the fact that they were both hit from the left. In the post mortem findings it says that Nermin Divovic was hit from the right-hand side and that the exit wound was on the left-hand side. One of the two is not correct. We do not have any indicators that would help us make personal opinions as to what is correct and what is not. In this case we can only rely on the law of probabilities. There are two documents which say that the bullet came from one side and the third document that says that the bullet came from a different side. If we look at the document where it says that Nermin Divovic was hit from the right-hand side, the probability that that may be correct is 0.5 and the other option is also correct to the same extent. If we look at the two documents which state that the bullet came from the left-hand side and exited from the right-hand side, according to the law probabilities, the correctness of that is 0.75. In mathematical terms and in terms of the law of probabilities, we should adopt the assumption that it is much more probable that they were hit from the left-hand side and that the exit wounds are on the right-hand side of their bodies. There are a number of other material facts that corroborate that, but they should be additionally corroborated by the forensic findings. On a video-clip that has not been used so far as far as I know, we can see Dzenana Sokolovic in the hospital and the video-clip also depicts the dressings on her wounds, based on which one could gain an impression that the right-hand side wound is lower on the body in respect of the left-hand side of the body, which shows that she was probably hit on the left-hand side of the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I now ask you to look at image 101, and before that can you please tell us what is officially said in the documents? What was the route that Dzenana Sokolovic and her son followed, and where were they when they were hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another very controversial situation. There are various pieces of information as to where they were hit and when that happened. According to one of Dzenana Sokolovic's statements, she was on her way back from Hrasno Brdo. She was carrying firewood. She had collected the firewood in Hrasno Brdo. And when they reached the building of Novo Sarajevo municipality, which is about 1.200 metres to the west, in the Street of Zmaja od Bosne they heard fire. They all threw themselves on the floor, and then she felt that she had been wounded. Later on she pointed to the place where she was hit on a video-clip that was recorded by the Prosecutor's office and she pointed to the plateau in front of the museum in Zmaja od Bosne Street. And then when she testified she said that she had been wounded when she stepped out on Franje Racog Street. A film that was recorded on that occasion shows the boy lying in the middle of the street, so she could not say with full reliability that that was indeed the place where she was hit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know where this is going but this is Mr. Poparic giving evidence as a fact witness completely inappropriately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, that raises an interesting issue because this clearly is an expert witness who was tasked with trying to establish how something occurred, and in the course of establishing how something occurred he's looking at scientific evidence but he's also looking, as he should, at other facts. And the Prosecution was allowed to have Barry Hogan, for example, to come and testify as to these similar kinds of things that led them to believe that it happened in the way the Prosecution's theory was. So we don't have the kind of resources or the big team that the Prosecution has, but it seems to me that there's nothing wrong with our expert who went to Sarajevo, who studied this whole thing, giving the same kind of testimony as Barry Hogan did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the notification? And could it not have been reflected in his report?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe that many of these things are in his report. I'm not sure about this particular one but when you -- in fact, this was one of the problems that you seemed to have with his report, that it contained comments on things that were outside of his expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance here? Paragraph 64 [as interpreted], footnote 288 speaks about that statement provided by Dzenana Sokolovic. Paragraph 163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, this -- his job in this analysis is not to provide an analysis of the credibility of witnesses who have appeared before other Trial Chambers. And I maintain my objection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paragraph number is 163, footnote 288 in the report. Could that please be corrected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please bear in mind Mr. Poparic was called as an expert, in particular a weapon and military equipment expert. Even if his report deals with some issues of credibility of other witnesses, the Chamber will not give much probative value to this, even if the Chamber did not order the redaction of that part. Bear that in mind and I will let you continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will try and stick to the ballistic theory as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what is claimed? How many bullets arrived and what kind of trajectory they followed? What did you conclude about the trajectory based on evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is claimed that one bullet was fired from the direction of the Metaljka building and that it hit Dzenana Sokolovic, that it pierced her belly and went through it and then hit Nermin Divovic below his right eye and then exited behind his left ear. However --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Let's just see one thing. Was it ever established what the level of entry and exit wounds were on the body of Dzenana Sokolovic on her belly?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was never established. If that had been established, it would be much easier to assess whether that claim is correct or not. Without that it is practically impossible to establish with any reliability where the bullet had been fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How can one explain the entry wound and exit wound on little -- on the little boy, whether it was behind the right ear and below the left eye or vice versa? How could that oblique trajectory be caused by a bullet piercing the mother's body?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very hard to explain. It's impossible to explain based on the assumption that a bullet had been fired from the direction of the Metaljka building. The trajectory from there or the angle would be 5 to 8 degrees, depending on the height from which the bullet was fired, and the trajectory would be from upwards to downwards. In that case, the entry wound on Dzenana Sokolovic's body would be higher than the exit wound, and that same would be applicable in Nermin Divovic's case. The entry wound would be -- below the left eye should be above the exit wound above the right ear. Based on the photos, one can cast doubts on that, which is why I repeat that the post mortem findings would be of some essence here in order to establish what exactly happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the second option and that is that she was hit when she was crossing the street. According to one finding she was hit in front of the municipality and according to another document she was hit when she was stepping on the other side of the pavement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at image 101. 101, page 146 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who does the photo depict, where they are standing, and what are the buildings that surround them?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building in the background on the right-hand side is the land museum in Sarajevo, and on the left-hand side the building is the school of philosophy in Sarajevo as well. And the persons we can see in the photo are Mr. Barry Hogan and Dzenana Sokolovic, and she is pointing to the place where she was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be assisted with the electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please make a circle around her feet, i.e., in the place which she claims is the place where she was hit, and can you put number 1 next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now I would ask you to look at Franje Racog Street from which you can see Metaljka, and can you please draw a line along that street?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That photo doesn't depict it very well, but that would be here more or less, behind the trees. That's where the Metaljka building is and I can draw an arrow pointing at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date and the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this as a separate document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3626, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, estimating Mr. Hogan's height, how far from that spot the pedestrian crossing is where the accident happened?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The pedestrian crossing is about 50 metres away or to the left of Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe you can indicate it with an arrow --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- showing the direction at which she was moving and --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the direction in which she was moving and in that direction there is also the pedestrian crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Relative to this photograph and under what conditions was there a line of sight between this spot and the Metaljka building?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to see a person standing here from the Metaljka building because that grove is very thick. Maybe you could see someone in certain positions, but on the whole it is difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please mark the height of the late Nermin with an upright line next to his mother, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- this line is a bit too low.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please date and sign it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps for the record it would be useful for Mr. Poparic to indicate the basis for his estimate of the height of the boy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The basis for an estimate of the boy's height is the photography taken at the pedestrian crossing where the boy was lying. There are those black-and-white stripes in the pedestrian crossing and they are -- and their width is standard. And so we established that the boy must have been 110 to 120 centimetres tall. We didn't know Mrs. Sokolovic's precise height either, so we had to estimate it. We did it based on the height of Mr. Hogan. We supposed his height to be 1 metre, 95, and the other day I had a conversation with the OTP and Mr. Hogan was present. I asked him his height and he said it was 1 metre, 93. Dzenana Sokolovic's height estimate relative to Mr. Hogan's height is sufficiently accurate for this -- for our purpose. Dzenana Sokolovic is about 1 metre, 65, tall according to our estimate, and the boy, between 110 and 120 centimetres, which is a point to -- with regard to the fact where the boy was hit and where Mrs. Sokolovic was hit, because there is incongruity there. If she is 165 tall and he, 110 or 120, then the bullet may have come from the right side, but then the boy should have been hit lower down his body. For a person 1 metre, 80, tall, the distance between his navel and the ground is 110 centimetres. And considering the photograph showing where Dzenana Sokolovic was wounded, it is very difficult to explain how a bullet fired from the position from which the OTP claims it was fired could have hit the boy. But if the boy was at a short distance from her, then it is possible for the bullet to have hit both her and him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You told us that the line was a bit too low. Could you draw again at a proper height.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can draw it like this. I was referring to the head, but I don't seem to be getting it right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I will leave it at that. Have we admitted this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment, please. Let's make this clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say that it would have been possible for the bullet to have come from the right or from the left?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the height so estimated, it is only possible for the bullet to have come from the right and continue to the left because the boy may have been at a certain distance from his mother and then the bullet's trajectory would have been such as to hit both the mother and him. And in the opposite case it was -- it is not possible because he is too tall for such a trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And whose positions were to the right from them and whose positions were to the left if they were going toward the centre?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The boy was to Dzenana's left. It is asserted that Dzenana was hit before the boy. If it was fired from the Metaljka building then he -- it was -- the bullet was in a downward trajectory. And if the boy was further away from his mother, he would have been hit even lower down his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? And then let's move on to see photograph 100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3627, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see image 100 on the previous page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is this photograph from and what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is from a video-clip made by some firemen who worked as a humanitarian organisation and who recorded some video footage. We see the boy, Nermin Divovic, lying on the pedestrian crossing. On the left there is a photograph seeing -- showing a stream of blood behind the left ear, and in the right photograph we see a wound under the eye and the fireman is pointing at that wound, which tallies with the official information that the wound was under the eye. We see here that the stream of blood behind the ear is thin and further down there is more bleeding and blood flowing. According to my information this was supposed to show that the wound of the left is the entry wound and the one on the right, the exit wound. I consulted a forensic medicine professor from the university, Dr. Jovan Dunjic - I believe that he will be an expert witness here as well - I wanted to check with him and he agreed with me. But he said he couldn't give a conclusive statement without more information. But he also agreed that the left-hand photograph shows the entry wound, whereas the other shows the exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the conclusion of the police -- of the first police investigation report?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- actually, the police only related the information they got at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If they are walking toward town, what was the direction from which the bullet flew both vertically and horizontally?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this photograph -- actually, if you watch the video-clip you can see it better and you will see that the wound is at the height of the ear, the centre of the ear. To me it seems that the left wound is lower down than the one on the right, but a forensic report would make things clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asking if he had described if the wound was from left down --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Now he's not only an investigator but also a forensic expert, Mr. Karadzic? Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I'm asking from the ballistic point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the direction of the bullet as described by the doctors on the day of the accident, and where must that bullet have come from and what was its trajectory? That's ballistics.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I reply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to this photograph, or rather, these two photographs we see right now, the bullet went downward on the vertical plain, and in the horizontal plain it went from the boy's back to his front.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And relative to the left and right sides of the body?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From left to right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then that opinion was changed. How many years later was it changed?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Nobody really changed their opinion. Only at General Galic's trial did Dr. Beslic say that he had examined Dzenana Sokolovic and established that the entry wound was on the right and the exit wound on the left. But he didn't make any specific conclusions. It would have been very useful if he had measured the heights of the entry and exit wounds respectively. But since he is a general surgeon, it probably didn't mean anything to him. A forensic medicine specialist, I think his name was Dr. Milos Savljevic, contested that after so much time it was impossible to establish which wound was the entry wound and which was the exit wound. That was the only new element in this evidence but that isn't very helpful because there are no exact indicators.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D07459, please. From the beginning to 12 seconds could we please play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please explain to us what we're about to see.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a video-clip made at the site probably by these firemen and it was evidence in the -- in General Milosevic's trial. You can see the site of the incident and the boy Nermin Divovic lying on the pedestrian crossing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Play it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this child was hit as this still shows on the pedestrian crossing?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And no aid was provided until this vehicle arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it seems so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does this physical evidence tell you about the site of the incident and the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one observation before I forget and it's important. The boy is lying on the side of the alleged entry wound. As we see, it's a child 110 to 120 centimetres tall. Based on our estimate his body weight is not great, but he was hit with a high energy bullet. It would have been logical for him to lie on the other side. That's one illogical element. The other is, still referring to this still, we cannot see the firewood anywhere that Dzenana Sokolovic was carrying. She said that she had carried firewood, but we don't see any on this pedestrian crossing. And the third illogical element which is also important to my mind, the beginning of the clip shows that the camera is on a plateau in front of the museum. These vehicles arrive and only then do we see the boy on the pedestrian crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this video has sound. I don't see why we, if we're going to be watching it, can't have the full picture, so to speak, and to have the actual sound of the video played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, certainly. But we needed silence in order to hear the witness's comment. We can re-play it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we switch to the e-court and Sanction again. Let's see whether it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can see through Judge Baird's monitor but I can't see it -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's leave it at that. At least we heard some sounds. And then I was told that the video itself has some problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The Prosecution can -- Mr. Reid can release the copy of the video that we have which doesn't have any problems, if it takes only a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue. We'll review it again later on if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON

utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic. But you have no objection to the admission of this video?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Video 1D7459 receives number D3628, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I haven't given notice, but if I'm allowed I believe that if we could get from Photoview Sarajevo something that would make it a lot clearer, map 7. Yes, map number 7, it's a photograph from the Holiday Inn. That would be helpful. We could ask Mr. Poparic to help us. Map 7 Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 92 ter 21216 -- 65 ter, I'm sorry. Shall we switch to e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we zoom in just a bit, please, but we need to see both Metaljka and this other area, please, just a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, could you please use different colours to mark where the child was, where one report says that they were hit, where another report says that they were hit, and where Dzenana Sokolovic herself says that she had been hit. You can use the same pen but different colours.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the film --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, that's completely outside of this witness's area of expertise. That's not what he's here for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I tend to agree with that. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. No, no. I can say this: From a ballistics point of view I have to put the question whether there is visibility in terms of Metaljka from which positions, because where Dzenana Sokolovic is standing one cannot see Metaljka and that is ballistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But how can this witness mark the position where the boy was reported to be?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw it on the film, the zebra crossing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But how can he identify the spot on this photo?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if I may, Dr. Karadzic didn't ask for him to mark just one spot; he asked for him to mark three spots.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution's own witness Van der Weijden basically did the same exercise. For example, where there's a 3-year-old girl that was shot through a balcony, he took reports as to the place where she was shot and then decided and told us how he thought there was a line of sight, and in other incidents as well. I don't see why this witness can't do the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without asking how he would be able to do that, he just asked to mark the places. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, Mr. Robinson in reply to you a while ago, he referred us to evidence given by Mr. Van der Weijden. Do you recollect his evidence -- what your recollection is matching what Mr. Robinson had said?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Have you any recollection at all of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I have his testimony in front of me, but I do have recollection. And what Mr. Van der Weijden did was he received GPS co-ordinates from the OTP as to identifying the specific incident location. He went to the incident location as identified in the GPS co-ordinates and in the case of this 3-year-old girl he attended that location in the presence of an eye-witness, who explained to him where the victim was standing at that time, and at that location went down to the level of the 3-year-old girl, observed the surroundings to see what the technical and tactical possible lines of sight were to that incident location. That's what Mr. Van der Weijden did. Here we have no indication that either this witness went to the scene of the incident to observe what was technical or tactically possible. And frankly, we don't have any indication if he's going to be talking about line of sight that he actually even went to the Metaljka building to see what could be seen from there. And in all cases Mr. Van der Weijden once he determined the tactical and technical possibilities went to those potential shooting positions, if I can call them that, or shooting areas to see if there was a line of sight from those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Robinson, the Chamber is clearly concerned about this situation. Do you wish to reply at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Judge Baird. Basically Mr. Poparic did the same thing. He went to these positions, he looked -- he looked at photographs, he looked at videos, he took the totality of the information available to us and made the same conclusions. I don't think it's -- whether he went physically to one site or another that goes to the weight. But he's giving the same kind of testimony, he's drawing conclusions based upon -- ballistic conclusions, line of sight, capability of weapons, based upon information that was collected and I think that that's the very same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you should have put to the witness as to what Mr. Robinson submitted before you asked the witness to mark certain position, in particular as to his ability or on what basis he would or would not be able to mark the position. And then you may do so, but it all -- but I have some doubt as to the weight of such evidence if he's not guided, for example, by some specific scientific data as to GPS numbers or something like that. Please continue. I hope you understood my point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. I wanted to ask him to show where Metaljka is, and on the basis of the material he received, I wanted him to pin-point the places where it is claimed that the victims were. And there are at least three places. Mr. Poparic did study all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When you answer the question, please explain to the Chamber on what basis you reached the point you are going to indicate. Do you understand, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. First of all, may I say that I toured these locations several times, so I was there on the spot and I saw all the possibilities in terms of where this place can be seen from, and I can confirm that this place is visible for -- from part of Metaljka. Secondly, the boy's position can be seen from this film and then there's also this photograph. I don't know whether we provided it. It's in the film. And according to the number of black-and-white areas, one can see that the boy is roughly in the middle of the street. So you cannot determine it exactly in terms of centimetres, but it's roughly around the middle. I also saw Mrs. Sokolovic's testimony and she indicated that she was on this plateau in front of the museum, and I think that there is also a photograph where that was marked. I don't know who marked it, whether it was the Prosecution or I don't know. Also, there is this testimony that it was towards the end of the sidewalk, the other side of the sidewalk. Now, why is the place where they were so important? It is important because of the angle of the trajectory in relation to the body. So what would be helpful here would be, for example, image 111. It has to do with another incident, but there is a picture of Metaljka and this particular place. Just to give you an idea of the angles, which is what really matters, that is possible, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just before we go too much further and we lose this, page 56, line 24, the witness said he saw Mrs. Sokolovic's testimony and she indicated she was on this plateau. She did not indicate that in her testimony. I believe he's referring to a video he looked at. And at page 57 where he refers to testimony, and I think we need to be completely accurate here, he's not referring to her testimony in the Dragomir Milosevic case but to something else; I'm not completely clear what.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Edgerton is quite right. I meant the video film taken by Mr. Barry Hogan. That's the film where she shows that she was on the plateau and describes all the circumstances under which she was hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should we then ask for the points to be marked? And he saw from the materials he saw that these are the places where it is claimed that the victims had been hit. I believe that that would assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us see how it evolves. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please activate the pen.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it has been activated. So in the video film the body --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we zoom in a bit further? That's enough, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here somewhere in the middle of the pedestrian crossing where I put number 1, that's where Nermin Divovic's body was lying on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can you put number 2 next to the crossing to the pavement on the other side which is mentioned in the police reports?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be here; right? I can use the same colour; right? Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find it somewhere in the documents that she was hit as she was stepping down from the pavement?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that she said it herself, that she stepped down on the street and that she had just made one step and she was hit. I can mark that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go on and mark it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How wide is this street?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 8 metres. You could even do the maths if you take into account white and black patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now show us where she was standing together with Mr. Hogan and where is it that she told Mr. Hogan that she was hit in front of the museum?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the historical buildings in the background, I would say that that was somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can you please mark the Metaljka building.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In accordance with your expert opinion, did that projectile arrive from the Metaljka building?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am basing that claim on all the available facts, on the basis of the estimate of the boy's height, the height of Dzenana Sokolovic, and the position of the wounds that can be seen in the video, and all that gives us a realistic assumption that they were hit from the left to the right as was written in the first couple of reports compiled by the police. I repeat once again that the final solution could be found only in a forensic findings for Mr. -- for the boy, Nermin Divovic, if such a report exists, and perhaps another overview of Mrs. Dzenana Sokolovic's wounds, if that exists as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please put the date on this photo and sign it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3629, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, was the video we saw a moment ago already admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, but the Prosecution has the original of this video, which was why I rose to offer up a better, clearer, audible copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was wondering whether it is identical with P2216. If you could come back later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I could tell you right now. One of them is a bit longer than the other one, and P2216 is shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll leave it at that. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, how much time do we have before the break, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, now can we focus on incident 17. Can you tell us in short what you could conclude based on the materials that were available to you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of March, 1995, in Sedrenik Street, the boy Tarik Zunic was wounded in the arm. He was on his way back from school.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we please ask for the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How was this incident presented and what did you conclude?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said that the boy was hit from the direction of Spicaste Stijene where the positions of the VRS were. However, in order to claim something of the sort, there should be some other evidence besides the fact that the boy was wounded. In order to determine the direction from which the boy was hit, it would have been indispensable to determine where his entry and exit wounds were on his fist. I was not aware of that, so it was not possible to determine the direction from which that round had arrived. All the facts point to a conclusion that at the time when the boy was passing along the street there was an exchange of fire. UNPROFOR reports and other documents testified to that. The Egyptian Battalion of UNPROFOR interfered in that exchange of fire. However, what is important for this case is that on that occasion, in the same street, another man was wounded very nearby, and that incident was in the indictment of General Milosevic. Bahir Bakta [phoen] was wounded and then that incident was omitted from the indictment. I don't know why. I believe that these two incidents were interconnected because there must have been a rather substantial exchange of fire in the area and the boy was probably hit as a result of that. But it's very difficult to say from whose side the bullet had arrived without a proper forensic investigation and a police investigation into the matter. The distance from which the boy was hit was over 700 metres, about 750 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at figure 115 in the document. In the Serbian version it's on page 165 in the document. Could you please tell us what the photo depicts, when it was taken, and who took it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photo of the positions of the VRS at Spicaste Stijene. The trenches are still visible there and so on and so forth. It was taken in the direction where the incident occurred in order to show approximately the visibility in that area. Once again when we're talking about the visibility, according to some testimonies there were some curtains along the street that protected the view of the street from Spicaste Stijene. So we don't know whether the boy was wounded behind those curtains or in front of them. He said that he had already passed the place where the curtains were; however, according to photo 113 we can see that that place is marked. I believe that he himself marked that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up photo 113 then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Previous page, page 164.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What do you see in this photo, and what do numbers 1 and 2 mark?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is the place of the incident as was marked by the person who was wounded and number 2 is the direction from which the bullet had arrived from Spicaste Stijene. I must say that he himself stated that he had passed by those curtains and then he was hit; however, when we inspected the area and when we toured the site, obviously with the police, the man who lives in the second house on the right-hand side with an identical roof told us that he personally had helped Tarik Zunic and he also described the entire event in a very similar way, as was presented by the police report. He described a massive shooting and he identified a place where Tarik Zunic was wounded as being very close to his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please activate the pen and mark the place where you were told the incident happened with number 3.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the place on the street. It's very difficult to mark precisely. In any case, I'll put number 3 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this change anything in terms of the trajectory and the visibility?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me say that in terms of visibility it does change the whole picture. We took a photo from next to the lamppost. It's very difficult to see in the background where Spicaste Stijene is. In any case, the visibility here is somewhat worse than in the other place. Now, a question arises as to what was the situation with those curtains, what about those curtains and where they were, but it's very difficult to answer that question. In any case, there was an exchange of fire. That was what was going on because another person was wounded, and according to all the documents there was an exchange of fire. As to who actually shot the boy, it is very difficult to determine that without the results of a forensic and a police investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please initial this photo and put today's date on it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This photo is not a part of the account of the incident, so I'll probably call it up later or I will just give up on it. Forensic analysis, not forensic and police analysis, line 15.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forensic analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you were able to conclude when you analysed the material available to you with regard to incident F16?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We shall assign a number for this image.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3630, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the original unmarked document has an exhibit number in this case. I'll just let Your Honours know as soon as I locate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of May, 1995, or rather, in March 1995 - it is on page 159 in the Serbian version, paragraph 191 in the English version - what was said about this incident and what is it that you established?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just one in a series of incidents where the main problem was to establish the place where the incident actually occurred. On the 3rd of March, 1995, a tram was shot. Two persons were wounded in that incident. One had been sitting and the other had been standing next to that person. According to the initial statement of one of the wounded persons, the tram was hit somewhere near a container which was part of a barricade near the Executive Council building or between the Executive Council building and the tobacco factory building.
