Later on that witness changed his statement and he claimed that the tram was hit at the crossroads of Franje Racog and Zmaja od Bosne Streets, and that it was hit from the Metaljka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at figure 111 and I will ask you to mark the places where the tram was according to the first statement and where it was according to the second statement. Figure 111, page 161 in Serbian. Thank you. Please carefully activate the blue electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just correct you. Not according to the first report, as you said it, but according to the first statement of the witness Alen Gicevic. According to his statement this is where the containers were and we have a video-clip to prove that. And the tram was hit somewhere around here, approximately here. And then it stopped at the place marked by number 2 next to the tobacco factory building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For the record, you have used the blue pen to show where Alen Gicevic said that the tram was at the moment when the bullet hit it, according to Alen Gicevic. Number 2?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 is where it stopped and number 3 is where the barricades were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 1 is the place where it was hit, number 2 is where it stopped, and number 3 are barriers.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And according to the official version, it would be here and that would be number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I asked you about numbers 1, 2, and 3, and it wasn't recorded, what you said.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is where the tram was hit according to Alan Gicevic's statement, when he provided his first statement. Number 2 denotes the place where the tram stopped near the tobacco factory. And number 3 denotes the place where the containers were placed. Number 4 is the place where the tram was hit, according to the official version of the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put today's date and sign the document, please. And then could you please tell us what do you agree with? In other words, what do documents and the physical evidence show?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3631, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the lower part of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you what your opinion is about the physical evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the photo documentation, which is not very good but still good enough for us to be able to spot the most important things, one can observe that the seat where the wounded Azem Agovic had been sitting was turned at the angle of 45 degrees in respect of the axis of the tram, in the area where it was, so that that wounded person, Azem Agovic, had been sitting at an angle of 45 degrees with regard to the wall of the tram. Based on that and based on the fact that his entry wound was on the left-hand side of the body and that the exit wound was on the right-hand side of the body, or at least that's what he said in his testimony, one could establish whether it was possible to hit the tram, or rather, for him to have been inflicted such a wound if the bullet had been fired from the Metaljka building and that was not possible. If the bullet had been fired from the Metaljka building he could not have sustained such injuries because he was sitting at an angle of 45 degrees in respect to the wall of the tram. If the seat was placed normally, then one could say that there may have been a possibility for that bullet to have come from the Metaljka building. Since there are certain ambiguous statements about the tram which may have already come out from the curve, that possibility of the bullet having been fired from the Metaljka building is completely excluded. It was absolutely impossible. It was demonstrated that the tram could have been hit only at a bigger angle if it was running parallel to the main street Zmaja od Bosne, and that could have been -- that bullet could have arrived from various directions, from the museum, from the Executive Council building, and so on and so forth. So this evidence demonstrates that the tram was not hit at the crossroads of Franje Racog and Zmaja od Bosne and also that it is most probably correct that it was at the place where that was mentioned by Azem Agovic -- no, not Azem Agovic, but by Alen Gicevic in his first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can I now ask you to use the red pen to draw the possible trajectories of the bullet in the case that the tram had been near the containers and also in the case that the tram was as the official version has it. We're talking about the horizontal plain, but also can you tell us whether there was also a vertical angle. In case that the tram was near the containers, where would the bullet have come from?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have come from this direction at an angle of perhaps 45 degrees or perhaps from this direction. That means that there is a cluster of directions or trajectories and those would be the outer limits of that cluster.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 1 next to that.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, let that be the cluster number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In case that the tram was where the official investigation put it before the S-curve - if it had been in the S-curve, things would have been different - but if it was in a straight line before the S-curve, can you please tell us whether there is an angle along the vertical line? Number 2 shows the direction from which the projectile had arrived if the tram was in the position where the official investigation put it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to establish the vertical angle. In any case, according to the description of the wound, it was not very large. It would have arrived from a lower height. The bullet would have come from a lower height, but it was impossible to establish that based on such a poor photo. It was impossible to establish the height. However, according to the description of the wound, the height was not substantial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Date and initial. According to your opinion, could this projectile have arrived from the Metaljka building?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. It could not have arrived from the Metaljka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you just explain one diagram for us and then we will go on a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3632, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the page be scrolled up a little, please. [In English] Could we lift the page to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, further. Image 112.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please explain to the Trial Chamber -- was this explained in the text?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably is but it may be better for me to explain once more. This horizontal black line is the hull of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please activate the pen. Please mark, starting with number 1, and explain to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1, hull of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's what the bullet hit first; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 2 indicates the chair, the seat, but this drawing shows that it was 300 millimetres wide. That is approximately the width of the body. We don't know the person's build exactly so that's why we applied a value with more tolerance. And the seat is positioned at an angle of 45 degrees to the tram hull, marked 3; an angle of 10 degrees, marked 4. These are the angles from the extreme left end of Metaljka; that is, from the extreme point of Metaljka to the normal of the tram, the angle is 10 per cent. That can be seen on image 111. That's that angle. If it enters the centre of the seat --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please mark it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll mark it 6. If we imagine a person standing here and being hit in the left hip as described, then he may have been -- then the trajectory may have been the left or the right limit of this angle. The same would have happened if we were to move this this way because a tram can move left or right. And if we proceed this way, then the exit wouldn't be on the right but in the front part, which shows that he couldn't have been hit from there given the wounds that were described. And 8, 8 degrees, this is an angle which shows the -- an extreme case. I'll mark it 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat this last explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters missed your last part, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was explaining this 8-degree [Realtime transcript read in error "80-degree"] angle. This is a limit value under which a person could be positioned and sustain injuries as described in the report. That is from left to right. That is a limit value which probably was much greater in reality. This degree --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: This angle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of 45 degrees is an average case where someone was hit in the left side and the exit wound was on the right-hand side. And now I can draw these -- the limits, the extreme values indicating a bundle of possible trajectories - I'll mark it 8 - but none matches this 10-degree angle, as you see. And I'll draw the position of Metaljka here. Metaljka is a bit longer, but the angles here on the right, as you can see on image 111, make this part here impossible. I'll mark this 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Line 12 I have a correction. The value is 8 degrees, not 80.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's 8 degrees. That's one possibility but obviously the angle is much greater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you said "normal angle," if the bullet had been shot from Metaljka, what -- under what angle would the bullet have hit the tram?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under an angle of 80 to 90 degrees. It can be -- I can tell from the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this what you meant when you said "normal angle"?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The normal angle is this left extremity of this 10-degree angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The right extremity, not the left one. Please date and sign this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this and I believe that we all deserve a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3633, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour and resume ten past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just another little -- for the record, another bit of cross-referencing. The photograph which the witness marked that was admitted as D3630, that's a marked version of P450 in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That means that Mr. Poparic didn't indicate the exhibit number when using the image. It could have been more helpful, but let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, I would like to go back to the beginning now. What can you tell us about incident F1, Anisa Pita? What was said and what is true? What did the physical evidence enable you to conclude?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This incident happened I believe on the 13th of December, 1992, and according to the indictment one bullet was fired from the positions of the VRS at the Baba rock and hit Anisa Pita, a young girl, in her leg, thus wounding her. This case was investigated in detail at the site and we wanted to find out whether there's a line of sight from the site of the accident to the Baba rock or Baba mountain. And we found out that there was not. We also checked the terrain profile based on topographic maps from three sources. One is the Military Geographic Institute in Belgrade, another map was made by an American institution, and the third source was Google Earth. In each case we came to the conclusion that the site was not visible, which means that the girl couldn't have been targeted deliberately from the positions of the Serbian army at Baba rock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see figure 32 which is on page 59 in Serbian. It's part of paragraph 28. Please remind the Trial Chamber in which position Anisa Pita was, how tall she was, and where she was hit.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was 3 years old. We don't know how tall she was. According to her mother's evidence, she had taken her shoes off and the bullet hit her heel. There is no other evidence from this incident. Allegedly the bullet was found but later lost. There is no medical documentation and so on. Only based on the statement of the parents, or rather, that's the only thing that we had, there was no physical evidence. But that was sufficient to establish that there was no line of sight, which was interesting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please explain what we can see on this map.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see part of the topographic map made by the military geographic institute in Belgrade. This orange line that there is -- one end of it marks the position at the Baba rock and the other ending in this red dot -- or does it? No, I apologise. At the end of this orange line there is the spot where Anisa Pita was. Based on this map we were able to draw, if we apply these altitudes, we were able to draw a profile of the terrain and about 2 metres of terrain block the line of sight between the two end points. And that matches the information obtained from other topographic sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What does this purple arrow indicate?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where do you see it? Oh, the purple arrow. This is the rough position of the hill or mound blocking the line of sight between the positions and Anisa Pita's position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The purple arrow indicates the terrain profile, this peak which is at this spot. There is also an enlarged portion because otherwise it would have been poorly visible given the scale. That's why it's enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What does this mean, 500-odd metres from Zagric to the rock?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer? And the speakers are kindly asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you repeat your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The distance of 403 metres is the distance between the site of the incident in Zagric Street, number 38 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the answer to the question what 500-odd metres from Zagric to the rock means.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a misinterpretation. I was asking about 403 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 403 metres, yes. That's the value given in the sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's the distance between this peak and the Baba rock?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which makes the total half?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over 900 metres, which fact shows how difficult it was to observe a small child at such a great distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Apart from the loss of the bullet and the absence of medical documentation, what makes you think that the bullet was not fired from Baba rock? Not only the line of sight, but what was the visibility like at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was most probably foggy. It was later said that the fog rose, but he was speaking about the place where he was, that he had gone to fetch water with Anisa. She was there for a while and so returned home with a friend. The fog dispersed soon, but whoever knows Sarajevo knows that Trebevic is a high mountain. So the fog can disperse but 100 metres above it can still be foggy. We don't know to what extent the fog really dispersed. Baba rock itself may still have been invisible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it possible for the child to be targeted deliberately and fired at from Serbian positions at Baba rock?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go to incident F2 of 17 April 1993. Can you tell us what was said, what's being alleged, and what the physical evidence told you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very similar case as the previous one. This is also about a little girl, albeit a bit older, who was playing in front of her house and hit by a bullet in her back. Fortunately she was only lightly wounded. According to the indictment the bullet was fired from the positions of the VRS at Baba rock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at your findings?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I apologise. I made a mistake. It's not Baba rock. It's Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at figure 34 which is at page 64 of the Serbian version, and in English it's in paragraph 35. No, it's paragraph 35, whereas the image is 34.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'm losing e-court all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The system seems to have a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can I please get image 64 [as interpreted] which is on page 63 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Image 34, page 63 in the B/C/S. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what this photograph is showing?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows the place where the house is located in front of which the girl was playing. It's the house in the background behind this red ellipses, behind the pink house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was the girl then? Can you activate the pen?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can't see the exact spot here. She was on the right behind the corner of the pink house in the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could any microphones that are not used please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're now looking at the transcript. We're looking at image 34 on page 63. Can I get the next image, please, image 35 on the following page. Image 34, page 63. We seem to be tired, all of us. Page 64 in Serbian and image 35. In relation to the position that the child was in and in relation to visibility vis-à-vis Spicaste Stijene, what would be noteworthy?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is noteworthy is the great distance involved, over 1.100 metres. It's very hard to see. There was no zoom when this photograph was taken and perhaps we might gain the impression of what it's like in the field, that it's very hard to see a child here. Regardless of all kinds of optical equipment and whatever, it would be very hard to target anyone intentionally under these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that trees had been cut down. Can you tell us in which part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left. It's like the letter S and to the left is the young forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When the trees were cut, were there any casualties on the Muslim side? In the evidence did you find anything?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find any casualties. I found some statements by Nedzib Djogo, I think -- no, Djozo, who said that he came there during the night and that he cut trees down but that they did not shoot at them [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once we see the image, could we please have the lower part of this page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that in line 11 it should have been "they had not been shot at."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is in image 36?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two photographs taken from two different places. The left-hand photograph was taken from Spicaste Stijene that was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska, and the one on the right was taken from Grdonj which was under the control of the BH army. As you can see, these red circles mark the place where the house is, the house in front of which this little girl was wounded. Both from Spicaste Stijene and from Grdonj the place is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are the photographs the same from the point of view of zooming?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the photographs with the same camera and with the same zoom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the lower part of the page now. I beg your pardon, page 65. Obviously something is not the same. Page 65, image 38. 38, image 38 -- actually, we can keep this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us what this depicts.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the possible directions from which the bullet was fired at this little girl. In the upper square we have an enlarged area around Spicaste Stijene where you can see the trenches of the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of BH. They can even be seen on Google Earth because there are lots of rocks there so you can see it very nicely. When we toured the area, we saw that the positions of the BH army were not only at Grdonj but they also had communicating trenches and dug-outs by Spicaste Stijene. That is 20 to 30 metres away from these positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. We presented that in our report. I don't know to which extent you can see that. They had these defence lines from the top of Grdonj downhill and then up Spicaste Stijene, almost up to the top of Spicaste Stijene. It's marked here. Those were the last positions of the BH army, so that's the last trench where the red line is, the last trench of the Army of Republika Srpska. I think there were four rather large trenches in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show the next image, 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us about the small one -- actually, we're still waiting for 39. First of all, this small image where we see 1 and 2, what does that depict?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 is the direction from the last trench of the Army of Republika Srpska marked on the previous image. And if we look at this enlarged area in the yellow square, we see that this direction crosses the neighbouring house that is in the immediate vicinity of the house where the wounded girl was. And now 2, that's actually several directions. These are directions that are trajectories between the houses. The first image where we saw the red ellipses, so that's the area, that's the directions, that's the view towards Grdonj that you can see through these houses, between these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Grdonj is under the control of ...?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army. So that is the photograph, the first one that we saw, 34. Through that area between the white and the pink houses, that's the view of Grdonj when you are watching from the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From a ballistics point of view can one determine beyond any doubt that this bullet had come from the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be absolutely determined that the bullet did not come from the Serb side, which is obvious in image 37, where you can see these places that are in the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska at Spicaste Stijene and the positions at Grdonj. As we can see in this image, the site of the incident cannot be seen when viewed from Spicaste Stijene, but from Grdonj one can see it. In all fairness, there is a biggish tree there, but the OTP explained that this was a smaller tree at the time, so during the time of the incident probably there was a clear view. But I personally think that no one intentionally targeted the little girl. I think it was a stray bullet. But it certainly could not have come from Spicaste Stijene, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I think that we calculated this. I cannot find it now, but that this house was supposed to be 40 or 50 metres away so that it could be seen, this area, because it is the house that prevents the view.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image 37, please. Page 65 in Serbian. The upper half or the upper third. Please zoom in so that we can see the two top photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain it now?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The left-hand photograph is the view from Spicaste Stijene from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. As you can see, you cannot see the ground floor of this building --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please carefully activate the pen and show us the site of the incident in both photographs.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident was somewhere down here and here. So the ground floor, we cannot really see that. There's this tree here so you cannot see it from the tree. But the girl was down there. She was playing where the ground floor is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see in the left-hand photograph, you can barely see the tree because it grew, and you cannot see the ground floor. You can only see part of the terrace. That is 2 and a half metres above the site where she was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put the date there and initial this.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3634, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now focus on incident 3, the 11th of July, 1993. Munira Zametica is the victim. Paragraph 39 in English and in Serbian of course, but in Serbian it's page 68 onwards -- no, 67 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it says with regard to this incident, how it is represented, and what you established on the basis of the material that was accessible to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11th of July, 1993, is the date of the incident when Munira Zametica was shot when she was fetching water from the Dobrinja river near a bridge on the river. According to the indictment, it is alleged that she was hit from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, from a church, as a matter of fact, the church in Veline. However, in the police report there is no reference to that, that she was hit from the church, but it says from the area around the church. If she was hit from the area from around the church, as is alleged by the police, then she could not have been hit from that position because the area around the church - I mean the ground floor - cannot be seen from the site. That can be seen in a photograph that was taken by the OTP. This bridge in Nikole Demonje Street makes it impossible to see the plateau by the church. It's impossible to check this nowadays because a building was erected in the meantime so this could not be checked. So if positions were, indeed, on the church, then there was this line of sight, but we do not know what the visibility was of the spot where Munira Zametica was. We don't know that for several reasons: first of all, because we do not have any reliable information about the time when this incident occurred; and secondly, the second reason is that we do not know what the river-bed was like. On the basis of the photograph that I mentioned a moment ago, it is obvious that the river-bed of the Dobrinja river had not had grass cut there. So there was quite a bit of grass there, and in July there's lots of vegetation there. So we don't know whether this vegetation sheltered Munira Zametica in a way or not. The second thing I mentioned, the time of the incident, that is very important because according to some official information the police registered that the incident occurred in the early evening hours, I think between 7.00 and 7.30 p.m. Then a witness, a woman, mentioned that the two of them had set out at the time when it was supposed to be night-time, so just before nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was the late Munira when she was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left bank, and this spot, the river-bank, cannot be seen from the church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I just note there's no French translation at the moment. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the bank could not be seen from --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the bank could not be seen from the church. When you start walking towards the river, you can actually observe the church from there. There were other people who were involved in the incidents. They went to get water, but they were behind the bridge so they could not be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish based on the documents whether Munira was hit as she was accessing the river or when she was returning from the river?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statement of the lady who was with her - I believe that her name was Sadija Sahinovic, yes, Sadija Sahinovic - Munira was hit as she leaned over to fill up her bucket with water. At that moment she was hit. She stood up and then the second bullet hit her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the investigation record on what side of the body was Munira hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no official medical documents showing on which side of the body she was hit. There is no forensic investigation about that, or at least we were not shown any such results but that would be very important. I would like to say that the bed of the Dobrinja river is covered with concrete. It is a concrete bed and she could have easily been hit by a bullet that ricochetted. According to the witness statements, on that day there were ongoing activities from infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that time were there any activities from infantry weapons when she was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When she was hit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've risen on this before but I'm going to do it again because I think this has gone over the top and too far. The evidence that's being elicited now from this witness is evidence on -- in fact, what you're being asked to do, Your Honours, is to prefer the credibility of this witness in his comments on the credibility of witnesses who have testified before your fellow Judges in previous trials before this Tribunal. He's -- there hasn't been a shred of ballistics analysis in the last two pages of transcript, and I think this is completely inappropriate for an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or Mr. Karadzic is wasting his time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Excellencies. I am interested to hear the witness say whether that was a sniper bullet which targeted Munira, whether there was visibility. I want to hear him say on what bank is the church, on what bank was Munira. If it was on the same bank, then the visibility was low. All that leads to a certain conclusion. The witness investigated everything. The witness read everything. That's exactly how the investigators --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Poparic was called as an expert witness on weapons and military equipment. I think Mr. Marko Sladojevic can give evidence to that effect as well if -- anybody can summarise what he studied and give evidence. It's up to you how you spend your time, but the Chamber is very much keen to hear some relevant and probative evidence from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And then I would like to call up P1739. P1739. The transcript is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you say? What is the distance between the place of the incident and the alleged place from which the bullet was fired?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we see here number 3. The place of the incident number 3, is it upstream from the bridge or downstream from the bridge?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Downstream from the bridge. We have to bear in mind that on the bridge there were some barricades made of sacks with sand some 2 metres high. At that time, at 1500 hours or at 1900 hours - it's really not important - they cast a shade because the sun shone from the right-hand side and I'm sure that the visibility in that area was much poorer than in front of the bridge --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which actually made it much more difficult to spot this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now could you please activate the blue pen and mark the place downstream from the bridge because what we see here is upstream from the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused and the witness please kindly be asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you put number 1 next to it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you check what we are missing from the transcript and repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is nothing missing from my last question and the gentleman's last answer. Everything is complete. I asked the gentleman to mark the spot downstream from the bridge and put number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you now put number 2 when you locate the church tower, and can you please mark that church tower. And in terms of the scale that you see in the left-hand side corner, could you please give us the distance between the two points?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The church could be here, somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that you will find it where it says "towers". "Towers".

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not appropriate. Coaching the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the map is in English. We should have it in Serbian, shouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the scale and tell us how far is it. Is it over ...

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see. It's about 1.100, as I've already told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the probability of an intentional targeting of a woman on the left bank below the bridge at 1730 [as interpreted] hours at such a distance?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the distance is 1.100 or even more metres than that, the probability of targeting that person is very low, even with a sniper rifle because its best results are at 800 metres. Anything over 800 metres yields somewhat poorer results. And now the question is what the visibility was at that time. That's a very important question, whether that shooter had the time to spot that woman and to fire within the interval of time while she was approaching the river to get the water from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said even with a sniper rifle. Do you have any doubts about the weapon being a sniper rifle? In other words, what did you conclude? What kind of weapon did he use?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the witness statements, I believe that there was a burst of fire. There are statements to the effect that bullets fell into the Dobrinja river. I don't see a reason why somebody would shoot into the river just like that, which proves that there were activities related either to that place or some other place and the bullets ended up in the river. I don't know what actually happened. However, I was on the church tower, in the church tower. I would personally never put a sniper there for two reasons. First of all, the space is very little in that tower and it's insufficient to secure the place with some sandbags or something else. Second of all, the distance from the position of the BiH army to the church is big enough to use the Osa rocket-launcher whose range is about 400 metres and to destroy this tower easily. In other words, whoever were to put a sniper there would be exposed to the danger of being destroyed very quickly. I said that even in the police report it doesn't say that fire was opened from the tower but from somewhere around the church so that the fire was opened from the ground around the church. And that place around the church is not visible from the bed of the Dobrinja river which you can see in the Prosecutor's photo which is not in my report although I should have probably put it in the report. I'm talking about the bridge in Nikole Demonje Street which covers the area in front of the church. You can see the top part of the church but not the bottom part of the church. In other words, if fire was opened from an area next to the church, there was no visibility there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 20 on page 87 could it say "1930" rather than "1730"; and in line 10, on page 88, the witness said that he did not believe that someone would shoot into the river using a sniper just like that, that somebody would use a sniper just like that for shooting into the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. A sniper is always used for a particular objective. A sharpshooter selects a target and that's the difference between a regular soldier and a sniper shooter. One would not just shoot into a river with a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D3635, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now please -- oh, sorry. We've already dealt with that. Incident number 5, could we please focus on that, the 2nd of November, 1993. It is Brijesce Brdo. Serbian page 79 and the paragraph number is 62, so in English it also starts with paragraph 62. What is being alleged in respect of this incident and what did you establish?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd of November, 1993, that's the date of the incident, and in my view this is an incident in the case of which no one can establish what actually happened on the basis of all the information available. Basically, all the information we had available was contradictory. There is no doubt that in this incident Ramiza Kundo was wounded. Now, where she was wounded we do not know. We do not know whether she was going to fetch water, whether she was wounded on her way back, whether a neighbour was with her and whether she was next to her. We don't know another important thing, namely, where the source was where she was going to fetch water. We don't have any medical confirmation in terms of the exit and entry wounds on her leg. As a matter of fact, there were even some contradictory reports as to which leg had been hit. According to the police report she was wounded in her right leg. What we managed to establish was that if she had been hit, as is most frequently claimed, from the area of Polje, where the positions of the VRS were, there is a possibility, or rather, this place is just as visible from the positions of the BH army that were in the immediate vicinity of the positions of the VRS, because in that area there was some separation line and that is confirmed by military maps and so on and so forth. So there is no information here on the basis of which one can reach a reasonable conclusion as to what it was that actually happened. We don't even know where she was wounded in the leg, how high up the wound was, because that is very important in this case because she claims that she was hit in a particular area. And that is flat terrain for about 10 metres and then it abruptly goes downhill from there. We need to know how high up her wound is on her leg and then we could check whether that part of her leg is visible from where the bullet had been fired. Because of this flat area, part of the leg maybe could not be seen and that could not be checked because there is no information as to how high up she was wounded. So practically no conclusion can be drawn here except for the fact that the place is visible from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and the positions of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please take a look at photograph 50. In the Serbian version it is page 80. That is paragraph 55. Can you tell us on the basis of this photograph where these Serb positions were from which the projectile allegedly came and what is the difference in terms of altitude?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's about 100 metres, the difference in altitude, and the positions from which they claim she had been hit are between Mrs. Ramiz a Kundo and Mr. Barry Hogan. That's where this should be. However, on the left-hand side where Ramiza Kundo is standing, the positions of the BH army are visible. They're to the left. So the separation line was roughly where the front of where Mrs. Ramiza Kundo's body is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please activate the pen and mark this in-depth where the Serb positions were, Polje as they call it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here, that is what is visible; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 1, what's the distance? So you said that the altitude difference is 100 metres?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The distance?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 600 metres. But all of this information cannot really be of any assistance to us because we don't have any information as to how high up she was wounded. You see this plateau where they're standing, it's practically flat. And then further down there is a slope and it's possible that the leg, or rather, the place where she was wounded was shielded in a way that could not have been checked because we simply don't have information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we know at least whether she was hit above the knee or below the knee?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She indicated below the knee. She roughly showed the middle of her leg in the film that we see here -- actually, the middle of the lower part of her leg to be precise. So that is why there is this reservation that it's possible that this was not visible from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This trajectory, or rather, exit/entry wound going through the leg, are they at the same level or is there a difference?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference would be slight here because the leg is relatively thin, say 10 centimetres, so a centimetre and a half or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a difference like that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't know. There is no information about the nature of her wound. Actually, we don't even know where the exit wound is and where the entry wound is and that's very important in this case. I beg your pardon. Here she is indicating that she had set out from her house towards the source, and then afterwards she said that she was walking from the water source to her house. So it's the exact opposite. We don't know what it was that actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just take a look at image 53 now so that you could give us a brief explanation about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 85 in Serbian within paragraph 52 -- no, 72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you tendering this marked image, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm sorry. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I sign this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sign it and put the date.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit D3636.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Image 53, please. Page 85 in Serbian. Paragraph 52 for the English version -- no, it is 72, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is on this map, Google?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a Google map. The red line shows roughly the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and the blue -- oh, I'm sorry. I've done something. And the blue marks the positions of the BH army. These lines were taken from that map of the Chief of Staff of the 12th Division. If it says "14" somewhere, that's a mistake. If it says the other number, that's wrong. So it is Rizvo Pleh who signed this. So this just follows approximately what is marked on that map so that we could have it on this map. F5 that is enlarged in this rectangle is the incident site as indicated by Ramiza Kundo in that film taken by the OTP. And if we look at these red shaded lines, those are the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska from which that site is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The red?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says "VRS." So that site is visible from there. As you look to the left, there is this natural obstacle, if you will, if we look at the enlarged detail by the house. It's like a pile of dirt. Whoever was there could see that and that's why you cannot see the site. That's why it's visible from the VRS positions only to a very small extent, whereas the blue lines, the shaded area, is BH army-controlled territory from which this site is also visible, what we can see here. So the area that was under BH army control is bigger, the area from which this could be seen, as compared to VRS-held territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. These two armies, do they have their positions on the heights there, or rather, on Brijesce Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS certainly didn't have their positions there; however, the BH army did have them. They had a tank there. Above from this place there's a church there and that's where a tank was. I don't know how many troops were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How do you know there was a tank, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ramiza Kundo confirmed, among others, that there was a tank behind their house and another witness. I believe that it was a military observer whose name was Brennskag, he also said. And since he was at Vitkovici, at OP4, he saw that tank and there are documents to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So now he's a summarising witness again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, very well. My intention, however, was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: About the angle of shooting, were both militaries in the same position to fire a horizontal bullet?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean by "a horizontal bullet"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were both armies in positions on elevated grounds in order to see the lower leg?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends on where you're shooting from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Whose positions are dominant in geographic terms?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In geographic terms the BiH positions are dominant. They are on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now could I ask you to focus on incident F6. Could you please tell us what was said about this incident and what were you able to establish?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident happened on the 6th of January, 1994. Sanija Dzevlan was shot with a single bullet while riding a bicycle across the bridge on Nikole Demonje Street. It is alleged that she was shot from the positions of the VRS from the direction of the church in Veline.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up image 55. In Serbian it's on page 99 and the paragraphs in question are 77 and 78, and further on -- 89. Page is 89 and the paragraphs are okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the Trial Chamber what the photo depicts?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photo of the bridge. I believe that the markings were made by Sanija Dzevlan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This is P2292, this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The blue circle marks the church in Veline, the church for which it is alleged that it is the place where the fire had come from. The black crossed lines mark the metal boards that covered the passers-by from anybody who would be able to see them from the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How tall were those metal boards in respect of the bicycle seat?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to testimonies, they were at least 2 metres high, which means that if a person is sitting on the bike they couldn't be seen from the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'd like to call up figure 59. What did you find out based on the physical evidence available to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the physical evidence available to me, i.e., the testimony of this person about the bridge being sheltered, or rather, the street was sheltered by metal board and about the place where she, according to her, was hit, we were able to establish when that spot became visible for anybody who may have been on positions by the church in Veline. And based on the distance between -- the distance that she was supposed to travel on bike from the moment when she became visible to the place where she was hit, we were able to establish that the bullet had to have been fired much earlier than she became visible to the shooter. That means that she could not have been targeted intentionally from those positions if fire was indeed opened from those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you remind the Trial Chamber what kind of wounds did the woman sustain? Do we have any information about the levels of entry and exit wounds on her body?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just a small thing, but again Mr. Poparic has said he came to his conclusions on the basis of the testimony of this person about the bridge and about the location where, according to her, she was hit, and his report is quite specific that he comes to that conclusion on the basis of a video, not on the basis of testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. In my mind, everything is testimony, but I suppose you're right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it who established that the person was hit as depicted in this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer you shortly, but before that let me remind you that when I said that the time that was needed for the bullet to travel the distance from the church to the place where she was hit is longer than the time that she needed to travel from the place where she was sheltered to the place where she was hit. I would also like to say that the highest velocity of that bullet M84 is the highest velocity. We don't know what weapon was in question. But I would also like to say that according to her own words there was a burst of fire because she spotted that there were ricochet traces on the asphalt. In other words, it was not a single bullet from a sniper rifle but a burst of fire. The wound was very peculiar and I have no medical information about that wound. Moreover, it is not even certain whether she was shot by one or two bullets. She said that there were two. Some medical documents show that she was shot with just one bullet through two parts of her back. I don't have any information about the wounds. We only know that none of her bones were injured, which is very difficult to achieve without hitting a bone. It seems more like a ricochet than a direct hit and that that only grazed her. We don't even have information as to whether the seat of the bicycle was damaged or not and it would be very important to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can we look at image 60 on page 93. Who took this photo and what it depicts, when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo was taken on 6th January 2012. It was taken by a friend of mine whom I asked to do that in order to save me the trip. He was a little late. He should have taken the photo some 15 or 20 minutes earlier. Still, it does carry a certain weight because it shows the weather and the conditions in Sarajevo around that time. It is dusk and all the astronomic data also corroborate that. Why is this photo important? It is important because in this case we don't know the exact time when the incident occurred. According to Sanija Dzevlan's testimony, the incident happened around 1630 hours and around another testimony it was between 1500 and 1600 hours. She claimed that she had set out to visit her mother in the hospital around 1500 hours and that hospital is some ten minutes away. So it is much more realistic to say the incident happened between 1600 hours and -- 1600 and 1630 hours. In my view that would be a more realistic time of the incident. However, we can see that at that time it is already twilight. It is possible to ride a bike. We took some photos to show the visibility, and it's about 400 metres, or rather, there is some visibility at a distance of 400 metres. But I don't think that anybody could have seen her from the church at that time of day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For the participants, figure 61 shows the exact time, 1630 hours.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two photos are the same but one has been cropped in order to show the distances between the facilities that are depicted on the photos. The other one shows the exact time. Figure 60 shows the time, 1641.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can it be claimed that that was an intentional targeting of the gluteal part of the victim's body?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. As I've already told you, the ballistics indicators show that the shooter had to have fired the bullet before Mrs. Sanija Dzevlan became a visible target, if she had ever become a visible target at all in view of the weather conditions and the time of day, which cannot be defined for that particular day. But in any case, it was twilight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it claimed that it was just a single bullet? And if that was the case, were you shown the levels of the entry and exit wounds on the person's body?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the available materials, I realised that there are claims about just one bullet. There are -- there is no information about the wound at all. We don't know where the entry wound was and where the exit wound was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What kind of medical documentation did you have at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just one report where it says that she was hit by a bullet in the back part of her body and that's all. And from that, one cannot conclude anything about the nature of the wound or the number of hits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can I draw your attention to incident number 7. Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it is time to adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought we were supposed to break off at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we had two half-hour breaks and we've been sitting already for 90 minutes. We'll continue tomorrow in the morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
